_about: Claims a news fact-check examined, with its verdict, both copied verbatim from the article (build.py checks every quote against the saved page). Only fact-checks that cover every candidate in a race. Verdicts are the outlet's own words: we never turn them into a rating. A verdict in several sentences is written with ' … ' between them; each part is checked.

articles.title: Fact-checking Becerra and Hilton in the California governor's debate on CNN

claims.claim: You dismantled the vetting that should have made sure that they were with a safe, protective family or sponsor
claims.verdict: Hilton stands on solid ground when he says Becerra's agency weakened vetting and lost track of thousands of children. He overstates it when he describes hundreds of thousands of missing kids and child sex trafficking.

claims.claim: Right now, because of your policies, we have the highest poverty rate and the highest unemployment rate in America,
claims.verdict: When it comes to the rates, Hilton is nearly spot on. … But pinning the blame entirely on Becerra's "policies" is a stretch, as larger global economic forces affect employment and poverty, and not just one political party's decisions.

claims.claim: You said that every farm worker in California should be deported.
claims.verdict: But he did not specifically say that every farm worker in California should be deported.

claims.claim: You said Trump's ICE immigration policies and his raids were - your words - perfect,
claims.verdict: Hilton has expressed support for broader federal immigration enforcement and said Trump's deportation campaign was going "perfect" during a Fox News interview early last year.
